pages.name: Chronology
pages.html:
Campaign chronology for the altered 350–351 AC timeline. The module calendar is the authoritative date/time display at the table.

DateEvent
348 ACWar of the Lance begins in the east; Raistlin remains a Red Robe.
349 ACSilvanesti invasion and Lorac’s Nightmare. Caramon and the companions travelling with the brothers die; Raistlin survives.
Late 349–early 350Raistlin exhausts conventional attempts to reach Caramon’s soul and discovers Fistandantilus research.
Early 350Par-Salian/White Robe restrictions escalate; Raistlin abandons Red and takes Black.
Mid-350Wayreth traps Par-Salian outside and recognises Raistlin as Master; Conclave later ratifies the fact.
18 Darkember 350Campaign opens around Ispin’s funeral in Vogler.
20–21 Darkember 350Road to Wayreth begins.
Late Frostkolt 350Party reaches Forest of Wayreth.
1 Newkolt 351Night of the Eye; White Robe candidate completes the Test; Level 5.
Early 351 onwardArcs II–VI progress dynamically according to travel, War State and campaign choices.

Calendar setup: the “Road to Wayreth · 18 Darkember” GM control must set 18 Darkember 350 AC; the conjunction falls after the year turns to 351.

pages.name: Using the Tracker Board
pages.html:
From Arc II onward the GM has a dedicated Campaign Trackers panel positioned directly above the calendar. It is GM-only and designed for adjustments during play.

Board Controls

  • Six compact tracker cards are visible together.
  • Use the range slider for deliberate changes or the − / + buttons for quick adjustment.
  • Shift-click − / + changes by 2 for major decisions.
  • Alt-click − / + changes by 3 for campaign-reframing decisions.
  • The book button opens this journal.
  • The panel can collapse to a one-line score summary.

Tracker Discipline

Change a tracker when a decision reveals a pattern, changes a relationship, or materially alters the war. Do not reward every polite conversation or penalise every disagreement. Most sessions should move zero to two trackers.

Tracker Values Are Not Player Morality

High Trust is not “good.” Low Control is not a victory score. War State is not XP. Values describe the state of relationships and systems so later scenes can respond consistently.

GM-Only State

The board is not rendered for players and all mutation methods require GM authority. Discuss visible consequences in fiction; do not reveal the hidden numbers unless you intentionally want a transparent campaign.

pages.name: Raistlin Trust
pages.html:
Measures whether Raistlin considers the party reliable agents, intellectual peers, companions—or eventual security problems.

Range: −10 to +10 · Start 0

BandMeaning
−10 to −5Security problem. He withholds plans, builds contingencies and assumes interference.
−4 to +4Useful agents. He shares mission information according to need.
+5 to +8Trusted. He explains motives unprompted at critical moments and accepts private challenge.
+9 to +10Inner circle. He risks vulnerability and may ask the party to judge plans before acting.

Increase

  • Complete difficult missions without needless secrecy games.
  • Tell him uncomfortable truths directly.
  • Protect his secrets when disclosure would serve only spectacle.
  • Challenge him with evidence and workable alternatives.
  • Protect Caramon as a person rather than leverage.

Decrease

  • Betray explicit confidence.
  • Leak information to factions without strategic reason.
  • Try to manipulate him through obvious emotional pressure.
  • Destroy research before understanding what it does.
  • Agree to a plan and sabotage it later instead of objecting beforehand.

Trust changes what he tells the party. It should never make him automatically agree.

pages.name: Raistlin Control
pages.html:
Measures how strongly Raistlin embraces domination as the answer to loss, danger and uncertainty.

Range: −10 to +10 · Start 0

BandMeaning
−10 to −4He has repeatedly seen consent, voluntary sacrifice and negotiated power work under pressure.
−3 to +3Unsettled. He chooses method by circumstance and can still be moved strongly either way.
+4 to +7Control feels safer than uncertainty. He increasingly treats refusal as a technical risk.
+8 to +10Dominion has become a principle: nothing valuable should be allowed to leave or disobey.

Increase

  • Endorse forced resurrection.
  • Use mind control when credible voluntary routes exist.
  • Advocate permanent demon-binding over bounded agreement.
  • Treat the Returned’s inability to refuse as useful.
  • Sacrifice freedom for security as a default solution.

Decrease

  • Demonstrate voluntary sacrifice that succeeds.
  • Build enforceable consent into dangerous magic.
  • Find compassionate alternatives that still solve the actual problem.
  • Allow refusal and live with the cost.
  • Show that negotiated power can survive wartime pressure.

Do not lower Control because the party tells Raistlin control is bad. Lower it because they give him evidence another method works.

pages.name: Influence, Bond & Accord
pages.html:
Three trackers measure the campaign’s invisible philosophical relationships.

Fistandantilus Influence · −10 to +10

How successfully the Dark One’s assumptions enter Raistlin’s thinking. At +4 his phrasing and research priorities increasingly mirror Fistandantilus. At +7 the handwriting convergence and “prepared trail” become difficult to dismiss. Reduce it when Raistlin or the party explicitly rejects possession as a principle rather than merely opposing Fistandantilus personally.

White Robe Bond · −10 to +10

Raistlin’s relationship with the White Robe PC. This is not romance unless the table creates that; it is ideological intimacy and earned respect. At +6 he genuinely listens in the Abyss. At +9 he asks their opinion before his worst irreversible choice. At −5 or lower he sees them as Par-Salian’s institutional rigidity wearing a new face.

Wayreth Accord · −10 to +10

Whether the Tower increasingly recognises the party as part of High Sorcery’s survival rather than merely servants of its Master. At +5 doors/routes open for them. At +8 the Tower has enough evidence to understand that survival of the Art may require preservation of autonomous practitioners, allowing it to oppose a Master instruction that would preserve magic only through absolute domination.

pages.name: War State
pages.html:
Tracks the strategic pressure of the War of the Lance across the campaign. Side missions matter because this value changes what later arcs look like.

Range: 0 to 10 · Start 2

ValueWorld Condition
0–2Rumour, mobilisation, mostly open roads.
3–4Refugees, checkpoints, rising prices, local collaboration.
5–6Fortified towns, papers required, villages disappear, strategic routes contested.
7–8Regions under Dragonarmy control, major defensive lines active, cities preparing for siege.
9–10Palanthas / High Clerist theatre in crisis; collapse possible.

Adjustments

±1 ordinary strategic success/failure. Save a supply line, lose a town, expose an intelligence cell, fail a convoy.

±2 major outcome. Preserve or lose a fortress, destroy a major enemy magical asset, save a regional evacuation.

±3 campaign-reframing. Fall of Palanthas, destruction of a Tower, collapse of High Clerist line, or equivalent.

Use in Session Prep

Before each Arc II+ session, read the current War State and alter one visible environmental fact: prices, patrols, refugee density, fortification, travel documents, available troops or confidence. This keeps the war persistent even during research/dungeon arcs.
